race_context: The offices on the state list belong to the Monroe-Gregg School District (M-GSD), which serves Monroe and Gregg townships in north-central Morgan County, including the town of Monrovia; the state list adds the county name {mgsd_district}{monrovia_town}{in_list}. It runs Monrovia Elementary, Monrovia Middle and Monrovia High schools {monrovia_town}. Federal data list 1,567 students and three schools in 2024-25 {nces_mgsd}.

Superintendent: Trent Provo led the district through spring 2026 {mgsd_min_20260112}{mgsd_min_20260608}. On April 13, 2026 the board voted 3-1-1 (Tom Kennedy opposed, Jack Elliott abstaining) on a personnel recommendation that board attorney Steve Harris said named Andrew Grismore associate superintendent with the intent to make him superintendent July 1, 2026, pending contract negotiations; the minutes say members discussed the reasons for their votes but do not record them {mgsd_min_20260413}. After a public hearing with no comments, the board approved Grismore's superintendent contract 5-0 on June 8, 2026 and thanked Provo, who was leaving {mgsd_min_20260608}. Grismore had been the district's Ready Schools coordinator and grant administrator {mgsd_min_20260309}.

The board has five members {mgsd_bylaw0141}. Members are elected under the district's organization plan on file with the state {mgsd_bylaw0142}; that plan was not available, so the number of residence districts and who votes in each race could not be confirmed. The current members are Brock Sears (president), Kevin Blundell (vice president), Ky Kizzee (secretary), Jack Elliott and Tom Kennedy {mgsd_board}{mgsd_min_20260112}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 1 (Monroe Township) and District 2 (Gregg Township), one member each, matching the state list's 'vote for 1' {in_list}. Sears and Kizzee took the oath as newly elected members in January 2023 {mgsd_min_20230109}. Sears was a District 1 candidate in 2022 {rt_2022}, and a GoodParty.org listing shows Kizzee as the District 2, Gregg Township incumbent with a 2023-2026 term {gp_kizzee}. Neither is on the 2026 ballot, so both seats will have new members; Justin Quinnette is the only District 2 candidate {in_list}.

Budget and the 2025 property-tax law: on April 13, 2026 the board approved, 4-1 with Elliott opposed, a plan for financial savings that Provo said was needed because of the legislative changes in Senate Bill 1, with a goal of finding savings without cutting the workforce; Provo said vacated positions would be reviewed before being refilled {mgsd_min_20260413}. A resolution to withdraw from the Public Employees' Retirement Fund was tabled 5-0 the same night, and on May 11 Provo said there was no plan to move forward with it {mgsd_min_20260413}{mgsd_min_20260511}. The board held its 2027 budget hearing September 14 and scheduled budget resolutions for October 5, 2026 {mgsd_ag_20260914}{mgsd_ag_20261005}.

Referendum: on March 9, 2026 the board voted 5-0 to hire Policy Analytics to analyze the district's financial needs related to an operating referendum and the potential effects for the district and taxpayers {mgsd_min_20260309}. No referendum appears on the agendas reviewed.

Outsourcing custodial and maintenance work: on March 9, 2026 the board voted 4-1 (Kennedy opposed) to table a $749,973.67 facility management contract with GSF Cleaning and Support Services so current employees could meet with the company first; on March 23 the four members present approved it 4-0 {mgsd_min_20260309}{mgsd_min_20260323}. A teachers' association representative told the board on March 9 she had concerns about delays in cleaning buildings and hoped the board would take the same care with any future reductions {mgsd_min_20260309}.

Facilities and finance: on April 13, 2026 the board revised an earlier bond approval so the remaining funds could be used for capital facility improvements and approved refinancing a 2016 bond, which Provo estimated would save $200,000 or more {mgsd_min_20260413}. On August 19, 2026 the board voted 5-0 for a $682,947 solar panel project on the high school roof, fully funded through Google's energy efficiency program, with estimated savings of about $46,000 a year {mgsd_min_20260819}. The district also accepted Google donations of $50,000 to its rainy day fund (January), $200,000 for the agriculture/FFA program and $10,000 for e-learning connectivity (May) {mgsd_min_20260112}{mgsd_min_20260511}.

Planning and other issues: the district held strategic plan community meetings in early 2026 that included a 2025 facility study, and hired Kaiser Consulting for strategic planning {mgsd_min_20260112}{mgsd_min_20260309}. Board members voted 5-0 in January 2026 to pay themselves $2,000 a year {mgsd_min_20260112}. In May a resident asked the board to let homeschool students who meet state athletic association rules play Monrovia sports; in August the board approved athlete handbook updates that included homeschool student-athlete requirements {mgsd_min_20260511}{mgsd_min_20260810}. Board Policy 9270 was approved 4-1 on July 13, 2026, with Kennedy opposed {mgsd_min_20260713}.

Split votes: most 2026 votes were unanimous; the split votes found were the March 9 tabling (4-1), the April 13 superintendent-related personnel vote (3-1-1) and savings plan (4-1), and the July 13 Policy 9270 vote (4-1) {mgsd_min_20260309}{mgsd_min_20260413}{mgsd_min_20260713}.

Forums: no candidate forum or questionnaire for this race was found. District 1 has three candidates on the state list: Carl Gilbert (listed as Republican), John Landis Dowell (Independent) and Sarah Ragsdale (nonpartisan) {in_list}.
